transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’ve had to be more in front of people at work lately, and I can’t stop focusing on this one part of my face that looks uneven in photos. Everyone tells me they barely notice it, but I see it right away.
Do you believe for certain that this part of your face is actually abnormal, even when other people tell you it looks normal?
I mean, I see it right away in photos. People tell me it’s barely noticeable, but it still looks uneven to me, and I can’t really stop focusing on it.
Do you find yourself repeatedly checking your face in mirrors or photos?

Yeah. Before I send event pictures or get on a vendor meeting, I’ll keep checking my face in my phone camera. I retake photos, tilt my head different ways, sometimes ask a coworker if I look weird. It can take up enough time that I get behind on my planning work.
When you’re in meetings or around other people, is your main fear that they’ll judge you because of how your face looks?
Yeah, I worry they’ll notice it. Since I’ve been more in front of people at work, I keep looking at that uneven part in photos, even though everyone else says they can barely see anything.
If you didn’t have this concern about that part of your face, would you still feel very anxious speaking in front of people?

I don’t think so. I mean, being in front of people at work is what makes me start thinking about it, but if I wasn’t so focused on that part of my face, I don’t think speaking itself would make me this anxious.
Are the mirror checking and photo retaking mainly because you’re worried about that facial unevenness?

Yes. I keep checking the uneven part in the phone camera and retaking pictures or changing the angle of my head because I’m worried it looks obvious. Sometimes I ask a coworker if I look weird. It ends up taking time away from my planning work.
Aside from your concern about that uneven part of your face, do you have other unwanted thoughts that lead you to do repetitive rituals or checking?
No, I haven’t really noticed other thoughts like that. The checking is mostly just about that part of my face.
Do you spend a lot of time worrying that there is something wrong with how your face looks, even though other people say they barely notice it or don’t see it?

Yes. Since I’ve had to be more visible at work, I keep focusing on this uneven-looking part of my face, especially in photos. I can stare at it for a long time, even though people tell me they barely notice it—or say they don’t see anything.
Do you think it’s possible that your face actually looks normal and that your mind may be magnifying this flaw?

I mean, maybe it could be normal, since everyone else says they barely see it. But when I look at photos, I can’t stop focusing on that uneven part. It feels really obvious to me, especially now that I’m in front of people more at work.
Do you ever avoid meetings, photos, or seeing other people because you’re worried they’ll notice that part of your face?

I haven’t really avoided everything, but it has affected work. I missed part of a planning deadline because I spent so much time worrying about how I looked in the event materials. Vendor calls and getting ready for meetings take me longer than they should.
Do you find yourself repeatedly comparing that part of your face to other people’s faces?

Not so much comparing to other people. I mostly keep checking my own face—on my phone camera, retaking pictures, tilting my head different ways. Before vendor meetings I’ll sometimes ask a coworker if I look weird. It can take up a lot of time and put me behind on planning.
Right now, how convinced are you that this part of your face truly looks abnormal?

Honestly, I’m pretty convinced when I see it in photos. I know people tell me they barely notice anything, but I keep looking at that uneven part and it feels obvious to me. Especially with work putting me in front of people more, I can’t really stop focusing on it.
When other people look at that part of your face in person, do they usually say they can see the unevenness?
Most people say they barely see it, or they don’t notice it at all. But in photos it still looks really uneven to me, and I can’t stop focusing on it.
Do you believe this part of your face definitely looks abnormal?
In photos, yes, it really does look abnormal to me. I know other people say they hardly notice it, but I keep seeing that uneven part, especially now that I’m more visible at work.
Do you feel that the amount of time you spend checking and worrying about that part of your face is excessive?

Yeah, I think it probably is. Before I send event photos or get on a vendor meeting, I keep checking myself in my phone camera, retaking pictures, tilting my head different ways, sometimes asking a coworker if I look weird. It can take long enough that I fall behind on the planning work.
Is your anxiety mainly about that uneven part of your face looking defective, rather than about being judged for other reasons?

Yes. It’s mainly that uneven part of my face. Since I’ve had to be more visible at work, I keep looking at it in photos and feeling like it stands out, even though other people tell me they barely notice it.
Has anyone else clearly told you that this part of your face looks abnormal?
No. People mostly tell me they barely see anything, but I still can’t stop noticing it in photos, especially since I’ve been more in front of people at work.
Has worrying about this part of your face significantly interfered with your work or daily life?

Yeah. I missed part of a planning deadline because I spent so much time worrying about how I looked in the event materials. And vendor calls and meeting prep take longer than they should because I keep getting distracted by it.
Has there ever been a time when you were completely certain that this part of your face looked abnormal, no matter what anyone else said?
I mean, when I see it in photos, I feel really sure it looks uneven. Even if people say they barely notice it, I keep staring at it and can’t stop thinking it stands out.
